sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for its proposed medium regularized LSTM model as a single model?
What word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank does the paper report for its proposed large regularized LSTM model as a single model?
Does the paper report word-level test perplexity on Penn Treebank for its proposed model in any setting involving dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports model averaging (ensembles) of regularized LSTMs, but does not report dynamic evaluation, cache/pointer, or fine-tuning settings for Penn Treebank perplexity.

sub_questions.q: What single-model Penn Treebank word-level test perplexities does the paper list for baseline methods?
sub_questions.answer: Pascanu et al. 2013: 107.5; Cheng et al.: 100.0; non-regularized LSTM: 114.5.
sub_questions.quote: Pascanu et al. 2013 107.5 Cheng et al. 100.0 non-regularized LSTM 120.7 114.5

sub_questions.q: How do the paper's proposed single regularized LSTM test perplexities compare with the listed single-model baselines?
sub_questions.answer: The proposed medium regularized LSTM (82.7) and large regularized LSTM (78.4) are lower (better) than all listed single-model baselines: Pascanu et al. 2013 (107.5), Cheng et al. (100.0), and non-regularized LSTM (114.5).
sub_questions.quote: Table 1 compares previous results with our LSTMs

sub_questions.q: What model-averaging Penn Treebank word-level test perplexities does the paper list for baselines and for its own regularized LSTMs?
sub_questions.answer: Baselines: Mikolov 2012 (83.5), Cheng et al. (80.6), 2 non-regularized LSTMs (96.1), 5 non-regularized LSTMs (84.1), 10 non-regularized LSTMs (80.0). Own: 2 medium regularized LSTMs (77.0), 5 medium regularized LSTMs (73.3), 10 medium regularized LSTMs (72.0), 2 large regularized LSTMs (73.6), 10 large regularized LSTMs (69.5), 38 large regularized LSTMs (68.7).
